title: fix(sse): deterministic chunking/framing for SSE streaming (partial JSON + delimiter ordering)
author: Ava Patel
description: Fixes several edge cases in the server-sent events (SSE) streaming path that could produce malformed or out-of-order partial-JSON events when payload delimiters and token boundaries align poorly. Root cause: the chunking scheduler and the framing layer had inconsistent assumptions about when to emit event delimiters versus token fragments which caused consumers to receive JSON fragments with delimiter characters in the wrong order (or missing delimiters) leading to parse errors in clients and function/tool-calling regressions. This PR consolidates framing responsibility, adds an explicit delimiter state machine, ensures token ordering is preserved across batching boundaries, and adds targeted unit + integration tests that reproduce previously observed failure modes. Backwards compatibility: unchanged public API; streaming wire format improved for robustness. Rollout: feature-flag guarded at runtime and enabled for prod after CI and canary pass. Related Linear tasks: ENG-2315, ENG-2390.

release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming edge cases that could produce malformed partial-JSON events. Improves robustness of streaming responses and tool/function calling over SSE. No API break.
notes: This addresses customer-visible incidents where streaming consumers would fail to parse events during high-concurrency workloads. The new Framer is extendable for future framing policies (e.g., newline vs custom delimiter). Canary rollout over one week recommended.
examples_of_issue: Scenario: long token boundary coincides with event delimiter producing '}{' ordering inside a single wire fragment which client parsers mis-handle.
Observed in internal canary and reported by support under INC-142 where the openai-compat shim dropped trailing delimiter in certain batching conditions.
